title: SDK Locale Adapter: prioritization matrix for language coverage, auth handshake, and streaming ergonomics
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Summary: We need a repeatable framework to triage SDK and client-library feature requests coming from enterprise customers focused on three correlated axes: language coverage (locale adapters and edge-case tokenization), auth handshake patterns (token rotation, SSO flows, mTLS scenarios), and streaming ergonomics (reconnect, partial-result semantics, backpressure). This ticket scopes the product-side prioritization matrix, acceptance criteria, and onboarding signals used to route PRs to ENG/design and to make go/no-go decisions for Dedicated/Private customers.

Context: Over the last two quarters we have seen a spike in ask volume from enterprise customers and platform partners: requests to add edge locale handling (Thai/Burmese/Bantu tokenization anomalies), explicit support patterns for rotating service tokens and long-lived SSO sessions, and finer-grained streaming controls (early partial commits, client-initiated cancel semantics). Many asks include security constraints and regulatory requirements, which increases implementation cost and cross-team coordination. Current intake is inconsistent: PMs file ad-hoc tickets, and eng teams receive varying levels of context which slows triage.

Goals:
- Create a lightweight prioritization matrix that ranks SDK requests by combined product value and implementation risk across the three axes.
- Define signals and minimum artifact set for triage: customer reproduction steps, threat model, sample PRD, and signal-to-migrate (e.g., percent of customers requesting locale X or percent revenue impacted).
- Produce deterministic routing rules to decide whether work is: backlog, gated-design spike, engineering spike, or immediate roadmap inclusion for Dedicated/Private.
- Reduce average triage-to-assignment time from current ~3 weeks to <= 7 days for enterprise-impacting requests.

Scope (what this ticket covers):
- Product: prioritization matrix, intake checklist, customer signals, and communication templates for PM/SE handoff.
- Design: ergonomic guidelines for streaming APIs (client cancel, partial frames, resumable streams).
- Engineering: define API compatibility considerations to include in request template (breaking change risk, semver expectations).
- Not in scope: implementation of language tokenizers or the work to change runtime kernels; those will be separate ENG tickets once prioritized.

Deliverables:
- Prioritization matrix document (google doc link in Links).
- Intake checklist template added to the SDK intake Confluence page.
- Routing rules RFC for PM/ENG handoffs.
- Pilot triage of 4 queued customer SDK requests using the matrix and a short retro.

Risks and tradeoffs:
- Strict prioritization may delay low-volume language fixes that are cheap but could be critical to a single enterprise customer. The matrix should therefore include a "single-customer veto" path for contracted customers.
- Requiring more intake artifacts will slow some customers; mitigation: provide a short PM-led concierge intake flow for high-value customers.

Success metrics: see success_metrics below.
acceptance_criteria: Prioritization matrix doc published and approved by SDK PM leadership
Intake checklist added to Confluence and referenced in SDK support templates
Routing RFC reviewed by Eng leads for runtime, SDK, and security
Pilot triage completed for 4 customer requests with time-to-assignment <= 7 days
One-page handoff template implemented in Jira/Linear and used in pilot cases
success_metrics: Median triage-to-assignment time reduced to <= 7 days
>= 80% of enterprise SDK requests include required intake artifacts after launch
Number of urgent re-prioritized requests due to missing security info reduced by 60%
technical_considerations: Authentication: rotation-friendly SDK surfaces (refresh callbacks, opaque credential objects)
Streaming: idempotent partial updates vs. committed final frames semantics
Localization: adding locale adapters vs. runtime tokenizer changes; prefer adapter shim unless performance/regression risk is high
Compatibility: avoid introducing breaking changes; prefer additive APIs and feature flags
Telemetry: capture signal tags (customer_id, locale, auth-pattern, streaming-mode) for triage dashboards
proposed_priority_matrix: Axis: Customer impact (single-customer revenue, active users, compliance requirement)
Axis: Implementation risk (runtime kernel change, cross-team coordination, security review)
Axis: Operational cost (monitoring, support burden, observability required)
Scoring: 1-5 on each axis; automatic escalation if Customer impact >=4 AND Implementation risk <=2
Veto paths: Contracted enterprise customers with SLA+ can trigger direct inclusion regardless of score (requires sales sign-off)
